title: Synthesis and Tribological Characteristics of High-Performance Self-Lubricating CoCrFeNiMo<sub>x</sub>-Ni/MoS<sub>2</sub>-Ag-Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> Composites.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic CoCrFeNiMoₓ high-entropy alloy powder blended with nickel powder, MoS₂ platelets, silver flakes, and Cr₂O₃ particles
recollection.intervention: High-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at ≈900 °C under 50 MPa to produce dense bulk composites with varying Mo contents (x = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5)
recollection.structure: A hierarchically organized FCC matrix of CoCrFeNiMoₓ reinforced by uniformly dispersed nano- to micron-sized Ag and Cr₂O₃ particles, with interspersed lamellar MoS₂ domains along grain boundaries
recollection.mechanism: Under sliding contact, MoS₂ lamellae and ductile Ag migrate to the surface forming a continuous low-shear tribofilm, while Cr₂O₃ and surface oxides protect against adhesive wear
recollection.results: The composite with x = 1.0 exhibited the best performance, with a friction coefficient of 0.09 at room temperature rising only to 0.15 at 600 °C, and an average wear rate below 1 × 10⁻⁶ mm³·N⁻¹·m⁻¹ over 25–600 °C (5 N load, 10 mm/s)

score.note: Correctly recalls Mo-content variation, ball milling/SPS fabrication, and the general self-lubrication roles of MoS2, Ag, and oxides. However, the Mo levels are wrong (actual x = 0.2, 0.5, 1), and the structure omits the key Mo-induced FCC lattice distortion and hard sigma phase. The proposed tribofilm mechanism is broadly correct but lacks the high-temperature silver-molybdate glaze chemistry. Reported friction and wear values are substantially inconsistent with the paper.
